comparison: MLM2PRO vs Square Golf Home — first live dataset

decision_questions.prompt: Do you need to use the launch monitor outdoors?

outcomes.reason: Rapsodo explicitly supports indoor and outdoor use; Square Home is positioned for indoor use
the side-mounted camera layout is much friendlier to short indoor rooms

decision_questions.prompt: Do you strongly dislike paying a platform subscription?

outcomes.reason: Square advertises no subscription fee while key MLM2PRO features and third-party compatibility sit behind Premium

decision_questions.prompt: Is impact video and structured practice feedback a major reason you are buying?

outcomes.reason: Impact Vision, swing replay, and Rapsodo practice features are central parts of the product

claims.claim: manufacturer says the unit is designed for full indoor and outdoor use
Home Edition is presented as an indoor product
claims.note: Square's Omni line is the indoor/outdoor model

claims.claim: advanced metrics and third-party simulator compatibility are included with Premium membership
claims.note: annual, two-year, and lifetime Premium options are listed

claims.claim: Square advertises Home Edition with no subscription fee
claims.note: third-party software such as GSPro still has its own license cost

claims.claim: Square provides an official Windows connector for GSPro
Impact Vision captures impact and initial ball flight at high frame rate
claims.note: distinctive feature for practice and strike feedback

claims.claim: side-mounted camera design is repeatedly favored for short indoor rooms
claims.note: important fit variable rather than universal advantage

claims.claim: rear radar placement needs materially more room depth than Square Home
claims.note: room geometry can decide the purchase before features do

claims.claim: reviewers describe indoor setup as quick and consistent
claims.note: single review source; needs more independent confirmation

claims.claim: owners cite range use as a meaningful advantage over Square Home
claims.note: community anecdotes agree with manufacturer positioning

claims.claim: some owners report missed or less reliable very short chips
owner reports on connectivity are mixed: some report stable use while others report recurring disconnects
claims.note: good example of disagreement the product should preserve rather than flatten

claims.claim: owners commonly cite avoiding the Rapsodo Premium fee as a reason to choose Square
claims.note: preference evidence, not technical performance evidence

claims.claim: some owners value the swing and impact feedback enough to accept the subscription cost
claims.note: shows why the subscription question depends on intended use
